title: Choose materials and plan a card stand
outcome: CONSTRUCTION: select materials and plan the build.
goal: I can choose a material and safe join, plan the parts and steps, and check a card mock-up.
success: I can link a material property to the stand purpose.
I can record sizes, tools and a safety step in my plan.
I can make a card mock-up and use it to improve the plan.
materials: Usually light and easy to fold. Thin card may bend or sag.
Useful for a small mock-up. Test the actual card.
A fluted middle often adds stiffness for its mass. Edges can crush.
Possible stand material. Compare the actual piece and flute direction.
A round rod, often wood. Its diameter affects its size and fit.
Would need a different approved design and safe prepared lengths.
Wood from certain kinds of tree. It is not always soft to touch or easy to cut.
May be stiff but needs a suitable revised plan and adult-approved hand tools.
A water-based glue that can suit some porous materials. Suitability varies.
Use only after adult label and material checks. Hold the join as directed and wait for full cure.
A heated adhesive join can bond some materials. Hot parts and glue can cause burns.
Compare only in this block. No hot-glue tool or heated adhesive is used.
material_note: These are model descriptions. The actual material, thickness, direction and adhesive label matter. A picture or model description is not a test of a pupil sample. Hand tools only. No powered or heated tool is used in this block.
safety: Wait for the adult to approve the actual material, hand tool and work area. No power tools or heated tools.
The adult checks scissors are suitable for the actual card or board. If cutting is difficult, stop; use adult-prepared parts. Do not force the blades.
Cut seated or in the agreed stable position, on a clear surface. Keep fingers clear. Close scissors for pauses and carry them only as the adult has shown.
Use the agreed cold join. For PVA, the adult checks the actual label and materials. Follow the stated handling and full cure instructions. Do not guess a cure time.
Hot glue is a comparison only. Do not plug in or use a hot-glue tool. Dowel or wood cutting is not part of the default card route.
For any concern, stop, put tools down and tell the adult. Restart only when the adult has checked and cleared the concern.
fallback: With no card, tools, paper or printer, hear the model material descriptions and written sizes. Point, speak or sign a material choice and reason. Rehearse the steps with empty hands. An adult records exact confirmed words when a recording method is available. Mark transcription pending until it exists. A card mock-up and material tests stay pending; rehearsal is not practical evidence.
careers: Construction designers and model makers choose materials, list parts and plan a safe sequence before a build. A small mock-up can reveal a change before more material is used.
vocabulary: A feature of a material, such as stiffness or how it folds.
A list of the parts, quantities and sizes needed.
A simple model used to check an idea before the main build.
A way to connect parts so they stay together.
When an adhesive has set fully as its label requires.
The order in which steps are done.

adaptations.Cognition and Learning: Read one material row at a time. Compare two options before more. Keep the cutting list beside the plan. Model one step with tool and safety, then fade to a prompt. Use a repeated stop and check routine.
adaptations.Communication and Interaction: Accept pointing, speech, signing and pupil-directed scribing. Give thinking time and offer two choices before an open question. Read a scribed choice back for correction.
adaptations.SEMH: Keep the brief about an invented client. Offer a private adult check and a calm pause. Put tools down before a pause and agree the safe return. An unfinished mock-up can show a useful next step.
adaptations.Sensory and Physical: Offer adult handling, prepared parts, large marks and an accessible ruler view. Do not force texture contact or tool use. Record which actions the pupil did and which an adult did. Rehearsal is not cutting evidence.
adaptations.EAL: Plan in any language. Pair the actual part with its size and material word. Use short chunks for material, property and reason. Preserve the pupil meaning in confirmed scribing.
adaptations.Literacy and Numeracy: Read each size with its unit. Find ruler zero and the same measuring edge. Use a completed example row, then cover it. Read tools and safety columns aloud. A calculator or adult can support the 260 minus240 tab check.

purpose: Invented client Sam needs one landscape paper prompt card to stay upright on a clear desk. The card is 80 mm wide and 60 mm high. The default body base is 120 mm by 80 mm. The whole stand, including the channel, should fit a clear table area 160 mm wide by 120 mm deep. Design a small tabletop stand that supports it for 30 seconds without a hand, is easy to move, and has no loose sharp parts. Do not use a phone, cable or personal item for the test.
dimensions: Default triangular tent stand: main thin-card blank 120 mm wide by 260 mm long. Measure crosswise fold lines 80 mm, 160 mm and 240 mm from the SAME short edge. Three 80 mm panels form a triangle; the final 20 mm tab overlaps inside. Card retaining channel 100 mm by 30 mm, folded lengthwise at 10 mm and 20 mm from the same long edge. Test card 80 mm wide by 60 mm high. Written measurements govern; diagrams are not templates.
parts: Fold across width at 80, 160 and 240 mm from the same short edge.
Two long folds at 10 mm and 20 mm from the same long edge make a shallow U.
This is the test load, not a stand part.
model_choice: Adult model: thin card for the Week 2 mock-up and paper tape for the cold join. Thin card is easy to fold. The triangular shape may hold the card upright. Test the actual mock-up. A final material change needs a revised plan and adult check before Week 3.
checks: Measure each cut size and fold mark. Aim within 2 mm of the written size; use a difference to improve, not to grade.
Check the tab is inside the triangle and the U channel has its back flange taped to the lower front face, a shelf projecting out and an upward front stop.
Use one landscape 80 mm by 60 mm card. On a clear level desk, support it in the U channel for 30 seconds without a hand. Stop if the stand tips or the card slips.
Record what really happened, one change and why. A planned test is not a completed test.
plan: Check the actual Week 1 design and sizes. Choose card and paper tape, or revise with the adult.
Ruler and pencil; material sample if available
Adult checks material, tool access and safe workspace first.
Measure the two stand parts and test card. Mark all fold lines from the stated edge.
Use ruler zero; recheck before any cut.
Cut parts with suitable scissors, or direct the adult using prepared parts.
Fingers clear; close scissors at pauses; never force thick board.
Fold at 80, 160 and 240 mm. Bring the last 20 mm tab inside. Tape the triangle closed.
Fold on the flat surface; no knife scoring or heated tool.
Fold the channel along 10 mm and 20 mm lines into a shallow U. Tape its back flange to the lower front face. Shelf out; front stop up.
Adult checks the shelf is out and the front stop faces upward toward the card.
Check with the test card for 30 seconds. Record one change and keep the final plan.
Test card and count or timer
Use a clear level desk. Hands away for 30 seconds; remove the card by hand. Stop if it tips or slips.

stages.name: Arrival
stages.title: Retrieve the design problem
pupil: Find your Week 1 design and specification.
The stand must hold one 80 mm by 60 mm card upright.
Today we choose materials and plan before the main build.
stages.teacher: Retrieve the actual Week 1 choice and any adult-approved revision. Read the invented client brief. If the prior record is missing, use the labelled adult model and mark the missing pupil design; do not invent an earlier choice. Describe the 30-second test on a clear level desk. Allow a calm settling pause inside the time.
stages.check: Ask what the stand must hold and how it will be checked. Expect one landscape card, upright without a hand for 30 seconds. Reread the brief if needed.

stages.name: Starter
stages.title: Which property helps the job
pupil: Compare thin card and corrugated board.
Thin card can fold; board can be more stiff.
Use a real sample result or name the model information.
stages.teacher: Show actual thin card and corrugated board if available. Bend gently with adult approval; do not tear or force. Read the model descriptions if samples are absent. Dowel and soft wood are alternatives for a different approved design; PVA and hot glue are joins, not sheet material. Hot glue is comparison only; no heated tool is used.
stages.check: Ask whether one model description proves the actual sample will work. No. Link a named property to a purpose, and keep actual sample results separate.

stages.name: I do
stages.title: Parts sizes and a safe plan
pupil: Watch the ruler start at zero.
Mark folds from the same short edge.
Write a tool and safety check beside each step.
stages.teacher: Show the main blank and the cutting list. Measure 120 by 260 mm. Mark crosswise lines 80, 160 and 240 mm from the same short edge, not 80 then another 160. Name three 80 mm panels and the last 20 mm tab. Show the 100 by 30 mm channel and 80 by 60 mm test card. Model one plan row with tool and safety, then leave a row for the group. Diagrams are not full-size templates.
stages.check: Ask the length of the last tab. 260 minus 240 equals 20 mm. Repoint to the same measurement origin if 100 mm or another value is given.

stages.name: We do
stages.title: Choose materials and compare joins
pupil: Choose a material for a card mock-up.
Use paper tape for the taught cold join.
Explain a property and a reason linked to the brief.
stages.teacher: Build a shared material, property, purpose reason. Default thin card folds easily; corrugated board may need adult-prepared folds or a revised plan. Paper tape joins the inside tab and channel. PVA may suit some materials but needs the actual adult label and full cure. Hot glue is not used in this block. Model why dowel or soft wood would need a new design, prepared lengths and adult-approved hand tools. Do not add sawing to this lesson.
stages.check: Accept another safe choice with a justified adult-approved plan. Check the pupil distinguishes sheet material from joining method and knows heated tools are not used.

stages.name: We do 2
stages.title: Stop before cutting
pupil: You marked 80 mm from one edge and 160 mm from the other.
Should you cut now, fix the marks, or guess?
Use the written sizes and the same short edge.
stages.teacher: Hinge answer is fix the marks before cutting. Put scissors down and remeasure both lines from the same short edge. If anyone chooses cut or guess, model ruler zero and the origin again. Parallel check: PVA feels dry; can you test it before the actual full cure is complete? No. The adult checks the label and full cure. Recheck after reteaching.
stages.check: Move on when the pupil can use the same origin and describe the tool or cure control. Otherwise keep Supported and adult-prepared parts; practical evidence must name actual support.

stages.name: Independent
stages.title: Plan and make a card mock-up
pupil: In your book, choose material and join with reasons.
List parts, quantities and sizes.
Write the steps with a tool and safety check.
Make or direct a card mock-up, then record what it shows.
stages.teacher: Use one route. Default mock-up uses thin card, paper tape and suitable scissors; pre-cut blanks may keep the task inside eight minutes. The pupil marks and folds with support, or directs adult handling. Close the triangle with the 20 mm tab inside. Fold the retaining strip along the two 10 mm and 20 mm lines into a shallow U. Tape the back flange to the bottom of the front sloping face; shelf OUT, front stop UP toward the card. Test only after an adult checks orientation and stability. If time runs out, keep the real stage and next step; never claim a finished mock-up.
stages.check: Check chosen material reason, three part sizes, plan tool/safety column, actual mock-up status and one real change or next check. Do not infer cutting if an adult supplied the parts.

stages.name: Review
stages.title: Use the mock-up to improve the plan
pupil: Test the actual stand with the paper card if ready.
Use a clear level desk and count 30 seconds.
Record one change or one check still needed.
stages.teacher: Check actual mock-up only if safe and ready. One landscape 80 by 60 mm card sits in the U channel without hand support for 30 seconds. No shaking, pushing or personal objects. A picture or imagined result is not this test. If it tips or slips, stop and use a real observation to plan an adjustment. Offer a private adult check; peer input is optional. Tidy inside the last minute.
stages.check: Pupil states what really happened and how the plan will change. A material-free route keeps mock-up and physical test pending, but can show a justified material choice and safe sequence.

stages.name: Exit
stages.title: Keep the plan for the build
pupil: I choose ___ because ___.
My first safe step is ___.
My mock-up showed ___ or is still pending.
stages.teacher: Retain the actual cutting list, sequence, material reason, mock-up status and next change for Week 3. Note which actions the pupil and adult did. Keep any cure or tool approval pending. Ask the pupil to confirm scribed words. Tools are returned and checked before leaving.
stages.check: Evidence is a pupil-owned material choice, measured list, safe plan and honest card mock-up record. The unit award is only named as the unit award; this lesson does not claim completion.

Supported: Read or hear the thin-card and paper-tape model. Say your own reason for each choice.
Use the partly completed cutting list. Find ruler zero and the same short edge.
Match one tool and safety check to each taught step.
Use prepared parts or direct adult handling. Record real help and keep unmade work pending.
Standard: Compare two materials and choose one with a purpose-linked reason.
List the main blank, U channel and test card with quantities and sizes.
Write a clear sequence with a tool and safety check for each step.
Make a card mock-up with approved tools. Record one real test result or an unfinished stage, then one change.
Stretch: Complete the core choice, cutting list, plan and mock-up record first.
Compare three materials and two cold joins. Explain a trade-off.
Explain why a thicker board could need a revised fold or adult-prepared part.
Predict a useful change from actual mock-up evidence. Keep any unperformed test as a prediction.
